shortDescription: Germany and France are expected to see higher electricity generation from wind and solar on Monday compared to Friday lows.($1 = 0.8586 euros)

children: Germany and France are expected to see higher electricity generation from wind and solar on Monday compared to Friday lows.
The German spot contract (TRDEBD3) was trading at €110 ($128) per megawatt-hour at 0824 GMT, according to LSEG data.
"Monday remains bearish as stronger renewable supply and softer demand sharply reduce residual load," LSEG analyst Naser Hashemi wrote.

Wind power generation is expected to rise by 4.4 gigawatts to 25.9 GW, compared to Friday levels, while solar power generation is expected to rise by 5 GW to 17.4 GW. Consumption in Germany is expected to edge down by 0.7 GW to 50.3 GW.
The equivalent French contract (TRFRBD3) was untraded.

In France, consumption was expected to edge down by 0.3 GW to 43.3 GW, wind power generation was expected to rise by 1.8 GW to 8.2 GW, and solar power generation was expected to rise by 0.6 GW to 6.1 GW on Monday.
French nuclear availability rose by 7 percentage points to 79% of total availability.

Operator EDF flagged that the third and sixth reactors of the Gravelines plant were shut down due to another large influx of jellyfish, while the first and second reactors were working at a reduced capacity as a precaution.
On the forward side, the German year-ahead contract (TRDEBYc1) was up 1.25% to €114.75/MWh, its highest level since November 2023.

"With European gas storages very low ahead of the heating season, Germany in particular is in a quite exposed situation, and it is therefore no surprise, that some of the country's most traded futures are trading around the highest levels since the energy crisis," analysts at Mind Energy wrote in a note.
The European carbon market's benchmark contract
edged up 0.46% to €82.80 a metric ton.
